segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״מֵת״ וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״לֹא מֵת״. זוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת ״מֵת״ — תִּנָּשֵׂא וְתִטּוֹל כְּתוּבָּתָהּ, וְזוֹ שֶׁאוֹמֶרֶת ״לֹא מֵת״ — לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא וְלֹא תִּטּוֹל כְּתוּבָּתָהּ.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» If two women who were married to the same man come forward, and «one» of them «says» that the husband «died, and» the other «one says he did not die, the one who says he died may marry» on the basis of her own testimony, «and she takes» the money of «her marriage contract. And the one who said he did not die may not marry, and does not take» the money of «her marriage contract.»

segments.he: אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״מֵת״ וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״נֶהֱרַג״, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: הוֹאִיל וּמַכְחִישׁוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ — הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ לֹא יִנָּשְׂאוּ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמְרִים: הוֹאִיל וְזוֹ וָזוֹ מוֹדוֹת שֶׁאֵין קַיָּים — יִנָּשְׂאוּ. עֵד אוֹמֵר ״מֵת״ וְעֵד אוֹמֵר ״לֹא מֵת״,
segments.en: If «one» wife «says: He died» in a normal manner, «and» the other «one says: He was killed, Rabbi Meir says: Since they contradict one another, these» women «may not marry. Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say: Since they both agree that he is not alive they may marry,» despite the fact that they dispute the circumstances of his demise. If «a witness says: He died, and a witness says: He did not die,»

segments.he: אִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת: ״מֵת״, וְאִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת: ״לֹא מֵת״ — הֲרֵי זוֹ לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא.
segments.en: or one «woman says: He died, and» another «woman says: He did not die, this» woman «may not marry.»
